chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed and Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
Regarding the drinker of wine: when he drinks, he is whipped. So if he repeats, he is whipped. So if he repeats, he is killed on the third (offence).
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Baseer, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them):
He said: 'The one who drinks wine, so whip him. So if he repeats, so whip him. So if he repeats, so kill him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for a person who drinks wine three times according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the graduated hadd punishment for the drinker of wine (khamr), prescribing flogging for the first two offences and execution (qatl) specifically on the third instance. While some jurists debate whether 'execution' here implies a distinct capital penalty or a severe flogging, the majority of Shia scholars, following the explicit wording of Imam al-Sadiq (AS), interpret it as a unique capital punishment for habitual drinkers who persist despite previous corrections. This ruling highlights the severity of alcohol consumption in Shia jurisprudence as a recurring sin requiring escalating disciplinary measures.
